tasks.short: Check signatures and required details on the occasional cheque received for payment.

steps.what: Inspect the cheque for required fields, signature presence and legibility.

loop.output: Field values, image locations and missing-field flags; signature presence only.
loop.check: Validate dates, amount agreement and required fields; retain image references. Never infer signature authenticity.
loop.stop: One extraction and one retry for unreadable fields; unresolved fields go to the billing clerk.
loop.why_not_simpler: Handwriting and variable layouts require document reading. Use existing capture configuration if it passes local validation.

steps.what: Compare payee, amount and payment reference with the receivable and payment instructions.
Assess signature concerns and alterations; decide whether to clear or query the cheque.
Record the disposition and route unresolved concerns to the finance team.

tasks.design: Store cheque images in the {DOCS}; bounded extraction prepares a checklist, and deterministic rules compare it with the {ERP}. The billing clerk approves the disposition before the {WORKFLOW} records it and routes exceptions; encourage bank transfers through existing payment instructions to reduce future cheque handling.
tasks.previous_blocker: Cheques are uncommon in many European companies. Low volume, handwriting and limited access to authoritative signature records weaken the case for bespoke automation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing capture components and faster integration development can reduce transcription and comparison effort. They do not establish signature authenticity.
tasks.still_hard: Recognising forgery, confirming signing authority and handling bank-specific acceptance requirements remain difficult. A short manual checklist may cost less at very low volume.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk recognises suspicious context and obtains authoritative confirmation instead of treating a signature image as proof.
tasks.altitude: The clerk spends less time copying cheque details and more time resolving questionable payments. Existing acceptance and escalation rights remain unchanged.

reach.task: Coordinate replacement payment when a cheque cannot be accepted.
reach.learn: Learn debtor communication, dispute handling and the limits of collection authority.

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit supports deterministic bank-line matching using payment references, IBANs or invoice numbers; this does not verify cheque signatures.
Cheque field extraction needs local validation; signature presence must be separated from authenticity.
The proposed time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: This is a conditional workflow for companies that still receive cheques; many mid-size European companies rarely do.
Today's verification stops at an internal disposition; depositing the cheque and posting settlement are separate tasks.
The clerk has delegated authority for routine acceptance and escalates uncertainty under existing policy.
GDPR applies to cheque images and payer data. Apply EU AI Act obligations where relevant and assess employee consultation under national rules.
Build ranges assume one receivables integration, existing document storage and a small capture service.
unknowns: Actual cheque volume, countries, currencies and bank acceptance requirements.
Whether cheque acceptance can be discontinued.
Available capture features, integration access and representative cheque samples.
Who may approve exceptions and whether authoritative signature records are available.
Retention requirements and applicable national consultation procedures.
research_questions: Does existing capture software reliably read local cheque formats and flag uncertainty?
Which checks does the receiving bank perform, and which remain the company's responsibility?
Does cheque volume justify capture integration over a configured checklist?
new_work: Review extracted fields and every acceptance disposition.
Resolve unreadable fields, mismatches and signature concerns.
Maintain acceptance rules, access permissions and retention settings.
Sample extraction accuracy after format or capture changes.

tasks.short: Clear minor printer or scanner faults and report equipment problems requiring repair.

steps.what: Read the equipment error and consult the printer or scanner fault guide.
Clear an accessible jam or perform another permitted minor repair.
Test the equipment and decide whether normal billing work can resume.
Send unresolved fault details and business impact to repair personnel.

tasks.design: Configure error-code lookup in the {HELPDESK}, linked to approved fault guides in the {DOCS}. The clerk performs permitted physical checks, then confirms a prefilled internal repair request that the {HELPDESK} routes to the repair coordinator.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical intervention cannot be automated through office software. Equipment guides and repair contacts are often separate from the billing workflow.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing knowledge articles, asset forms and ticket routing can remove guide searching and repeated fault descriptions. No model loop is needed.
tasks.still_hard: Jams, worn parts and intermittent faults require physical inspection. Older equipment may provide little usable diagnostic information.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk judges whether a simple intervention is appropriate and whether the equipment actually works afterward.
tasks.altitude: Physical troubleshooting remains part of the clerk's week, with less searching and reporting. No additional repair or spending authority is gained.

reach.task: Compare recurring equipment downtime with repair and replacement costs.
reach.learn: Learn to measure downtime, distinguish repair costs from disruption costs and compare replacement options.

evidence.claim: Configured knowledge articles, asset forms and routing can reduce fault-reporting effort; physical jam clearance remains manual.
The digest supplies no documented equipment-repair automation case for billing clerks.
The proposed time shares, remaining effort and build ranges are planning estimates, not measured results.

assumptions: The equipment is an office printer or scanner, represented by {OTHER}, rather than specialist machinery.
Time shares describe a fault requiring escalation; successful minor repairs end after the equipment test.
A usable {HELPDESK} and approved fault guides already exist; direct diagnostic telemetry is unnecessary.
The repair request goes to an internal coordinator; authorising external repairs remains a separate action.
GDPR applies to named ticket records. Assess employee consultation under national rules if new logging changes staff monitoring; no model is proposed.
unknowns: Equipment types, fault frequency and permitted clerk interventions.
Availability and quality of fault guides and asset records.
Existing {HELPDESK} access and repair routing arrangements.
Whether ticket logging changes employee-data practices or requires consultation under national rules.
research_questions: Can existing {HELPDESK} configuration provide error-code lookup and prefilled repair forms?
Which recurring faults should bypass clerk troubleshooting and go directly to repair personnel?
new_work: Keep equipment guides, asset details and repair routing current.
Confirm fault descriptions and test results before submitting repair requests.
Review recurring faults with the repair coordinator.

role.altitude: For these two supplemental tasks, the clerk gains time from document preparation and fault reporting. Payment acceptance judgement and physical equipment work remain human responsibilities, with existing decision rights unchanged.
reach: Support bill and account collectors with clear replacement-payment cases.
Help budget analysts assess recurring equipment disruption.
skills_to_grow: Review document extraction against original evidence.
Handle payment exceptions and recognise limits of signature verification.
Use structured equipment diagnostics and repair requests.
Measure exception volumes and downtime before proposing further automation.
role.ambitious_version: Help the finance manager assess whether retiring cheque acceptance and reducing paper-dependent billing would remove more work than further automating these small tasks.
